text: Tata Stee! completed acquisition of Corus on 2 April 2007, at the peak of the boom that ended with the Global Financial Crisis in 2008, from which the world economy never recovered. in fact Tata Steel had acquired Corus at almost 34% higher valuation than its original offer price. Corus was later renamed as Tata Stee! Europe. : An important factor in Tata acquisition of Corus was its ownership of two hugely successful proprietary technologies. One was HybrelTM, a first in plating strip steel, a coating that combines properties of both metal and particles. The other was Ymagine, a new generation light gauge, pickled and oiled steel used in automotive and construction sectors. Such proprietary technologies would allow Tata steel to charge a hefty premium where normal steel had become a commodity item sold only at the lowest price. Ymagine was strategic to Tata Steel considering every vehicle produced in India had some amount of Tata Steel. However, by 2008, cheap Chinese steel dumped across the globe had rendered the business unviable. The company (Tata Stee!) was now exploring all options for portfolio restructuring, including the potential divestment of Tata Steel UK, in whole or in parts. The decision to sell the UK business came at a time when the global economy was staring at a further recession, this time driven by a Chinese meltdown. Questions based on the passage above:
